name: piston_crank
story: The flywheel turns two times. The crank pin goes round, the connecting rod rocks, and the piston slides 50 mm up and down the barrel: the slider-crank turns rotation into a straight line and back.

steps.title: Open the Dynamic Simulation environment
steps.command: Environments tab > Begin panel > Dynamic Simulation
actions: Click the Environments tab, then Dynamic Simulation.
steps.note: Dynamic Simulation works out how an assembly moves, and the forces and speeds as it moves.

steps.title: Turn constraints into joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Settings
actions: Click Simulation Settings and tick Automatically convert constraints to standard joints. Click OK.
Open Standard Joints in the browser to see the joints Inventor made from your assembly constraints.
steps.note: Parts held together with no movement between them become one rigid group, listed under Welded group.

steps.title: Crank, rod and piston joints
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Joint panel > Insert Joint
actions: Revolution joint: frame bushes to crankshaft. Revolution: crank pin to big end. Revolution: gudgeon pin to small end. Prismatic: barrel bore to piston.
Weld the key and flywheel to the crankshaft, the cap, bolts and nuts to the rod, and the rings, pin and circlips to the piston.
steps.note: Inventor warns of a redundant constraint in a closed loop like this; let it make the piston joint a Point-Line.

steps.title: Turn the flywheel
steps.command: Right click the crankshaft Revolution joint > Properties > dof 1 (R) > Edit imposed motion
actions: Tick Enable imposed motion. Input Grapher: 0 at 0.5 s and 720 degrees at 8.5 s.
steps.note: Stroke = 2 x the crank throw = 2 x 25 = 50 mm. Look at the graph: the piston moves faster near the top than near the bottom, because the rod is not infinitely long.

steps.title: Run the simulation
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player set Final Time to 9 s and Images to 450.
Click Run. The assembly moves and the timeline fills in.
Use the slider to scrub back and forth.
steps.note: Press Play below to run the same motion here.

steps.title: Plot the results
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Results panel > Output Grapher
actions: Under Standard Joints, tick the position of the piston joint.
The graph shows each value against time. Click on the graph to move the simulation to that moment.

steps.title: Record a video
steps.command: Dynamic Simulation tab > Manage panel > Simulation Player
actions: In the Simulation Player click Record (the red dot) and choose a file name and format.
Click Run again. Inventor saves a video of the motion for your portfolio.
steps.note: You can also export a moment to Stress Analysis (Export to FEA) to check a part at its highest load.
